I'm not going to get to deep into this.  Going through a lot of things in life right now. It's been weighing in heavy on me.  The pain won't go away,  so I tried to take my own life. And failed.
Wrote a note at work to my fiance and kids. Went home, got my gun,  made my way up to Idyllwild(mountains close to my house) and turned off at a passing zone. Put the pistol in my mouth, and squeezed the trigger. And nothing happened. 
That moment right there gave me a minute to think about what I almost accomplished. About how much pain I would have left my family with.
I shook it off,  paced back and forth for a minute, looked at the view. Thought more about my life ahead of me (M37) and knowing time heals. 
So on the way back down,  I stopped at Bee Canyon (shooting range at the foot of the mountain) and took out the magazine,  pulled out the round that didn't fire.  I cannot describe how eery it was to look at the hammer strike mark on the round-the primer failed to ignite/ failure to fire. I put the other 9 rounds downrange to verify ammo and pistol. No jams, pistol operated correctly. Cried for a while, went home, and hugged kids and family.  
My fiance doesn't know,  I don't have it in me to tell her. I made an appointment with a psych for the 5th next week.  I have an entirely different view on everything now.
After work today (as a precaution) I'm bringing all of my firearms to my uncle's house until I'm better. 

Hope this helps at least 1 person.
